//: RULES ARE DEPLOYED FROM HERE (T105). `firestore.rules` and `storage.rules` below point at the PRODUCTION rulesets, firestore.rules.prod and storage.rules.prod, and the merge workflow deploys them with `--only firestore:rules,storage`, after the functions and before Hosting. They must never point at firestore.rules or storage.rules: those are the PERMISSIVE EMULATOR rulesets (`allow read, write: if true` and the like), and deploying either would open the production data to anyone. The deploy job refuses to run unless these two keys name the .prod files.
//2: The emulators do not read this file: they run from firebase.emulators.json (scripts/start-dev.ps1, `npm --prefix firebase run test:functions`), which has no Firestore rules key, so the Firestore emulator allows all reads and writes, and whose Storage key loads the permissive storage.rules. Starting the emulators from THIS file instead would enforce the production rules against dev data and refuse the sample-data tooling's writes.
//3: To test rules against the emulator, load a ruleset per scratch project id: PUT http://127.0.0.1:8080/emulator/v1/projects/{projectId}:securityRules. functions/test/rules/ does exactly that for both .prod files.
//4: TWO HOSTING SITES (T118). `muninn-quest` carries the custom domain muninn.quest, which is where the site lives. `dnd-campaign-companion` is the project's default site: its web.app and firebaseapp.com addresses cannot be removed, so it answers every address with a 301 to the same path on muninn.quest. Checked on a preview channel of this site (2026-10-07): the query string survives, which invite links (/join?...) and sign-in links (/auth/link?...) depend on; the reserved /__/auth/ paths (handler, action, iframe) are still served, not redirected, so the action links in emails already sent keep working; and `/` needs its own rule, because `/:path*` does not match it. The Hosting emulator applies no redirects, so a change here is checked the same way: `npx firebase hosting:channel:deploy <name> --only dnd-campaign-companion --expires 1d`, then curl it. The site still uploads the build, because a site must have content to deploy. A plain `--only hosting` deploys both; PR previews deploy `muninn-quest` alone (`--only hosting:muninn-quest`; the CLI matches a site id like a target).
